title: Slide back along the curve

panels.title: Food gained per 10 machines given up

readouts.l: Food gained on the last step
Machines given up per extra tonne of food

predict.q: The economy starts at F (50 machines, no food) and moves back towards food, 10 machines at a time. The food gained for each 10 machines given up…

options.s: stays the same at every step
options.fb: That's a straight-line PPC. This curve bows out because workers are not equally good at both jobs.
That mixes up the two directions. The first workers moved back are the best farmers, so the first step gains the most food. Look at the bars: each is shorter than the last.
The steps gain 50, 40, 30, 20, 10 tonnes: each extra tonne of food costs more machines (0.2, 0.25, 0.33, 0.5, 1).
The bars fall at every step on a bowed-out curve; the curve gets flatter all the way back to A.

task: Move the **Machines** slider down from 50 and watch the food-gained bar for each step. Then switch on **"resources equally suited"**.

target.do: Move the Machines slider down to 20 or below (toggle off), then press Check.

takeaway: Rising opportunity cost works in **both** directions. The more food is made, the more machines each extra tonne costs. On a straight line the cost is **constant**.
explore: Switch on "resources equally suited": the curve straightens and every step gains 30 tonnes.
